rule:
Step 4, task 1: the layer's particle-size spread as a sample property, derived in closed form.

certification: TEMPORARILY_UNCERTIFIED_EMERGENCY_2026-09-30.  derived: true.  fitted: false.

Nothing from a drying curve enters any parameter.  Inputs:
* the size statistics of Faner et al. (2019) Sec. 3 (paper/analysis/datasets/faner2019_v2/conditions.csv):
  Deq from image analysis ranged 0.5 to 4 mm; 97.1 % (sunflower) and 95.1 % (soybean) of the particles in
  1 to 3 mm; average Deq 1.81 and 1.77 mm; sphericity 0.74;
* step 1's film derivation (evidence/derive_film_2019_*.json): the measured constant rate by item 05's rule
  (least-squares slope over the samples with X > 0.2388), the model's T_b, dh_vap, the secant cp, T_g, the
  dry mass per volume 1159.65 kg/m3, the declared sphere R_d, the Coletto pair's h at R_d;
* the Coletto B.7 to B.10 pair (export src/dtdc_simulator/core2/particle/bed_film.py), evaluated at every
  class radius with the same source state as engineering_foundation.source_correlated_film_pair();
* the model's remainder 0.020466 kg/kg (wet_core partition at T_Gamma, step 3 S1) and, for the march-shaped
  variant, the step-3 baseline marches B01/B02 (runs/B0*_steps.jsonl) and their derived core ends;
* the measured sample times and reading half-widths (evidence/onset_reading.json) for the step-2 onset rule;
* the measured references of the comparison (crossing, 0.10, plateau end), used only for comparison.

Film per class (closed form of the model's Ackermann balance): m' dh = h beta/expm1(beta) (T_g - T_b),
beta = m' cp / h  =>  m' = (h / cp) ln(1 + cp (T_g - T_b) / dh), so the Ackermann factor is the same for
every class and the class rate r_i = 3 m'_i / (rho R_i) is linear in the multiplier.

usage (PYTHONPATH export/src): python step4/derive_ensemble.py
